title: Seeing Is the Easy Part
concept: MIT Technology Review's October 19th feature on Arctic wildfire and permafrost carbon, checked against Earth Fire Alliance, XPRIZE, Alaska Public Media and Woodwell. A faced satellite, the Eye, looks down at one hot square on a cold false-colour plate. The film follows that square from a FireSat frame, to a seventy two hour clock on the Yukon Flats, to a plunge through the floor into two ground cuts side by side where a thaw probe stops at one foot on unburned ground and goes at least three times deeper in a burn scar, gives the fair doubt about suppression its own cold scene and a fought against left split, then a fork with three roads, fight, leave and set, a mild fire as an idea, and a dashed plan for next spring that lifts to a dashed ember square in orbit.

fingerprint.palette: orbital navy void with river cyan, a bright warm thermal amber and ember yellow hot pixel, ice cyan permafrost, peat brown, smoke wisps, dashed bone plan lines, low sunrise light and birch green on tan for the last frames
fingerprint.light_story: an orbital plate where one warm square is the only light, a clear ice-cyan cut for the doubt, then low sunrise spring light and one small ember flame
fingerprint.metaphor: one lit square seen from orbit that is first found, then timed, then buried, then forked, and finally a dashed plan

palette: orbital navy void with river cyan, a bright warm thermal amber and ember yellow hot pixel, ice cyan permafrost, peat brown, smoke wisps, dashed bone plan lines, low sunrise light and birch green on tan for the last frames
divergence_note: The last four films were a paper form in a snowy cutaway building, a plumb bob in dark ground with a steel bit, a calf on a pewter beach and a manila folder on a walnut desk. This film is a navy orbital plate with self-lit thermal colour, then a plunge through the floor into ice and peat, then low spring ground. There is no desk, no paper, no lamp pool and no cutaway building, and its dominant POV is looking down from orbit. HONEST OVERLAP: its hero is a faced object for the third film in a row (Plumb, Dotty, now the Eye), and its middle is a ground cutaway with a steel rod like 10-22's drill bit. The cutaway is held to one two-up shot of about twelve seconds plus a cold doubt scene, the rod is a faceless hand-pushed probe that stops, and the accent is amber and not vermilion.

treatment.winner: The Dramatist's one falling lens from orbit to soil to orbit with the Explainer's 50 versus 4 smoke and coin comparison and probe cutaway, the Enthusiast's three-way fork, and the Comedian's decoy squares gag cut to the XPRIZE scoreboard (the comedy stops before the doubt).
treatment.why: The story is a view from space that falls to the ground, so a faced satellite and a single hot square carry the argument in one picture a muted viewer can read: the square is found, timed, buried, forked and planned. The doubt gets a drained cold scene at full strength.

angle.thesis: Alaska is where machines are learning to see every fire, but seeing is only the first step. Deciding which fire to fight is still a seventy two hour human rule, and the choice has three branches, fight it, leave it, or set a mild fire on purpose.
angle.falsifiable_by: A working triage tool or any tested rule better than the seventy two hour call already choosing which Alaska fires get fought, or a published result showing suppression clearly does not change outcomes (which would make the question moot), or the planned cultural burns turning out not to happen.
supporting_facts: c10 FireSat protoflight caught the Moran and Chicken fires in one image
c6/c5 the Yukon Flats pilot attacks a fire only if crews believe they can contain it within 72 hours, on 1.6 million acres
c18 Edward Alexander, 'We need mild fire, not wildfire.'
c13/c14 the XPRIZE finals in Alaska asked for detect and suppress in ten minutes, AURA met the detection gate
angle.counterpoint_honored: c17 Michelle Mack: it is not clear suppression can have any impact on these fires. The film gives it a full scene (the test) so 'leave it' and 'set it' read as real options and not failures. The EDF triage tool (c16) and the CATG burns (c19) are drawn as plans, never as done. No claim says any AI tool is used in Alaska fire management and no XPRIZE suppression result is claimed.
angle.second_movement: The probe scene recontextualises the first: the loss is the ground, not the acres (c7, c8, c9), which is why choosing matters and why 'which fire' is the whole game on four percent of the money.
angle.throughline_object: the hot pixel (one lit square seen from orbit). States: a single hot pixel (c10), a pixel with a 72 hour clock, a pixel sinking into the ground, a pixel on a three way fork (fight, leave, set), and the final state is a DASHED ember square inside a dashed boundary, planned and not lit (c19 is a plan).
angle.ai_link_wording: Satellites (FireSat), the XPRIZE autonomous-detection contest in Alaska, and a PLANNED EDF AI triage tool. No source says AI is used by Alaska fire agencies today and the film never says it.
angle.valence: curious, leaning hopeful. The seeing is real and arriving, the deciding is open, nobody is a villain.
angle.one_question: When satellites can see every fire in the Interior, who should decide which ones get fought, which get left, and which get set on purpose?

runner_ups.enthusiast: credulous, gives detection a job no claim backs and sidesteps Mack
runner_ups.skeptic: accurate but sour, reads an absence as a verdict

hook.frame1: A black-indigo top-down false-colour grid of cold tiles with one amber square snapping on at frame 6 with an overshoot and a pulsing heat ring, the faced Eye sliding in from the top edge to look at it.
hook.headline: ONE SQUARE · ONE FIRE
hook.loopback: The last frame is one dashed ember square on the same cold grid, inside a dashed boundary, with the Eye blinking calmly beside it: the square that was found is now a plan.

open_loop.what: Somebody has to decide what to do about the fire. Planted as the reticle clamps on the pixel and a question mark rises, answered with three branches at the fork and handed back to the viewer as the closing question.

open_loop_2.what: Did anyone put it out? Planted as the XPRIZE put-out ring stays empty after detection, paid when the doubt line holds that suppression's impact is not clear.
